title: HarborWave onboarding: implementation ignition & runbook alignment
summary: Kickoff for Redwood integration at HarborWave. Discussed deployment models (dedicated vs hosted vs private VPC), data residency and KMS, runbook ownership, initial P0 success criteria (100ms median latency for 512-token seq on routing use-case, 99.9% availability for inference endpoints), timeline for pilot (4 weeks), and a bench of next steps: share dedicated sizing worksheet, security artifact pack, schedule smoke test with sample traffic. Action items assigned for both sides.
topics: deployment choice: dedicated vs hosted vs private
security controls: KMS / HSM, audit logs, SOC2/ISO
networking: VPC peering, firewall, egress rules
integration plan and data flow (prefix caching, KV cache reuse)
action_items: Maya Chen - send Dedicated sizing worksheet and cost estimate (due 2026-07-16)
Diego Ramos - prepare short smoke-test harness and example traffic script (due 2026-07-20)
Sarah Kim - provide compliance questionnaire answers and call out any 3rd-party KMS constraints (due 2026-07-18)
Tom Alvarez - confirm networking maintenance window and provide IP allowlist (due 2026-07-19)
Priya Nair - schedule weekly pilot sync meetings (first one 2026-07-21)
Lena Park - share sample prompt set (50 items) for quality monitoring and evals (due 2026-07-17)
next_steps: Redwood to send security artifacts link (SOC2, penetration test summary, SOC2 scope) and Dedicated sizing doc
Schedule pilot kickoff next Tuesday (2026-07-21) for smoke test with sample traffic
Agree on success criteria and test plan in shared spreadsheet
Customer to provide allowlist IPs and KMS constraints
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Diego, Priya (Redwood) — Lena, Tom, Sarah, Benji (HarborWave)

Summary (auto): Quick intro, technical intake, and alignment on pilot runbook and success metrics.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone uh thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. quick roll call?
[00:07] Lena Park: yep lena here, hi all.
[00:09] Tom Alvarez: tom here — platform.
[00:11] Sarah Kim: sarah, security.
[00:12] Benji Cole: benji, sre.
[00:14] Diego Ramos: diego — solutions eng at Redwood.
[00:16] Priya Nair: priya, cs.
[00:18] Maya Chen: perfect. objective today is to align on the implementation runway, network/firewall requirements, security checklist and the pilot success criteria. we'll also share the runbook owners and the testing plan.

[00:35] Tom Alvarez: quick context — HarborWave handles routing recommender models for last-mile deliveries, we have bursty traffic around shift changes and need consistent p50 latency under 120 ms for 256 tokens, p95 ideally under 300ms. cost is a factor but reliability is primary for us.

[01:02] Lena Park: and we also want to keep model outputs in-house, so the private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) is very interesting. we have on-prem GPUs but limited ops bandwidth.

[01:20] Maya Chen: understood. we typically recommend three patterns: hosted (fastest to start), dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our infra for predictable throughput), and private (VPC/private appliance). each has tradeoffs on onboarding time, ops overhead, and control. for your p50/p95 numbers — that will affect the sizing.

[01:50] Diego Ramos: just to add, for the routing use-case latency is very sensitive to KV cache hit rates and prefix caching. if you can identify stable prefixes we can leverage Redwood's prefix caching to cut token generation time. also quantization choices here will affect both cost and latency.

[02:18] Benji Cole: real question — we need to know how keys are managed, we can't have plain text keys stored in third-party. do you support customer-managed KMS or an HSM?

[02:28] Maya Chen: yes — we support bring-your-own KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated via customer KMS integration, and for Hosted there are options to integrate a customer's KMS for certain secrets; i'll send the KMS integration doc. (note: transcription might say 'kay em ess' in the recording)

[02:47] Sarah Kim: are audit logs available? we need per-request tracing and logs retained 12 months.

[02:55] Priya Nair: yep, Redwood Console has per-route tracing and you can configure log retention. we'll share the data retention and log export options — you can push logs to your SIEM.

[03:20] Tom Alvarez: networking, we need to know IPs, egress ranges; any chance to do VPC peering or VPN?

[03:28] Diego Ramos: we support VPC peering for Private and Dedicated, and for Hosted we provide NAT egress ranges and allowlisting. we'll document the IP blocks. if you need VPN we can work through SRE.

[04:01] Lena Park: timeline — how long to spin up a Dedicated pool vs Private?

[04:08] Maya Chen: Dedicated usually 5–10 business days after contract and sizing confirmed; Private (VPC) can be 2–4 weeks depending on network, and on-prem appliances 4–8 weeks. initial pilot we suggest Dedicated to minimize ops while giving you control.

[04:35] Sarah Kim: what about SOC2/ISO compliance artifacts — can you share scope and third-party pen test results?

[04:40] Priya Nair: absolutely, i'll drop the security pack after the call (SOC2 report redacted, summary of pentest, encryption at rest/in transit details).

[05:02] Maya Chen: P0 success criteria proposed: 1) pilot endpoints achieve median latency <=100ms for 512-token equivalent with your sample traffic, 2) availability >=99.9% during test window, 3) end-to-end tracing and logs exported to HarborWave SIEM. is that reasonable?

[05:28] Lena Park: 100ms median might be ambitious for 512 tokens but for our routing case we often have shorter sequences; could we set a sequence-targeted metric — 256 tokens p50 <=120ms, and 512 token median <150ms?

[05:45] Diego Ramos: that sounds practical. also we can provide suggestions for batching policy to reduce cost while meeting latency SLOs — adaptive batching with max batch window 10ms for your burst patterns.

[06:10] Benji Cole: do you do graceful fallback if a model fails? we need deterministic behavior not a cascade of errors during peak times.

[06:17] Maya Chen: yes — Redwood has smart routing and fallback policies. you can configure route fallbacks to smaller models or cached responses; also circuit-breakers and request queuing policies. we'll show the runbook and default fallbacks.

[06:45] Tom Alvarez: sample data — we will not send PII, but there may be hashed identifiers. any special handling?

[06:53] Priya Nair: logged — hashing is fine; if you need additional tokenization rules we can work on that during the pilot.

[07:10] Lena Park: okay let's talk about runbook ownership — who runs the smoke test and who triages?

[07:18] Maya Chen: typical setup: Redwood SEs help run the first smoke test and hand the runbook over to your SRE team. after that we co-monitor for one week then transfer ownership. action items will reflect that.

[07:35] Diego Ramos: i'm planning a simple harness: replay of 5k requests over 10 minutes with rate shape to simulate shifts; we'll provide both a cold-warm sequence and a steady-state. i will attach the script to the drive.

[07:52] Tom Alvarez: can we do a dry run in a staging VPC first?

[07:58] Diego Ramos: yes, staging VPC is recommended — we'll set up endpoints in staging and you can iterate.

[08:10] Sarah Kim: question about encryption— are your logs PII redacted before they leave your infra?

[08:18] Priya Nair: we have logging filters and can mask tokens and user content by default for Hosted. For Dedicated/Private, you control retention and export. we'll document options.

[08:35] Maya Chen: ok i want to walk through the proposed pilot timeline: week 0 — finalize sizing and network allow-list; week 1 — spin up Dedicated pool and deploy model variant (we recommend a quantized variant for the pilot); week 2 — run smoke tests and quality evals; week 3 — stabilize and iterate on batching/cache; week 4 — handoff and go/no-go.

[09:05] Lena Park: that timeline seems fine. we do need to align on the model variant — we're likely to use an open LLM (community) 16B variant; does Redwood support that?

[09:15] Diego Ramos: yes we support many open models and can onboard custom models. we will validate performance and recommend quantization profiles — e.g., 4-bit llama-family quantization with KV cache support. some model names may be mis-transcribed but we'll upload the exact binary.

[09:38] Benji Cole: retention — can we set different retention for traces vs full request bodies?

[09:43] Priya Nair: yes trace metadata and full request bodies are separate. you can set retention independently and configure exports.

[10:00] Tom Alvarez: about observability — does Redwood provide per-token latency breakdowns?

[10:06] Diego Ramos: yes per-token cost and latency breakdowns, token-level tracing, plus dashboard for per-route metrics. we'll show the console in the demo next week.

[10:25] Maya Chen: i want to call out some gotchas — network egress can add 20–40ms depending on region, so doing VPC peering often reduces latency. also cold-starts matter if the model is large and cache empty. we can set warmers.

[10:52] Lena Park: okay, so for pilot do VPC peering to minimize egress. Tom — can you get the peering request ready?

[10:58] Tom Alvarez: yes i'll validate with networking and share details by monday.

[11:10] Sarah Kim: also compliance: we need to know data residency — some customers require EU-only. harborwave has EU PO boxes; right now our cluster will be US-based but we may need EU soon.

[11:20] Maya Chen: we have regions and can pin deployment regionally; we'll note EU region availability and the timeline.

[11:33] Diego Ramos: small note on perf testing — please include a mix of long and short sequences in the sample prompt set. long tail sequences expose KV growth and memory pressure.

[11:48] Lena Park: got it. i'll prepare 50 prompts across categories and share.

[12:00] Maya Chen: let's talk about runbook steps — i'll quickly outline: pre-flight (network, keys, model artifact), deploy (model rollout, health checks), smoke test (traffic replay, latency and errors), observability (dashboards and traces), rollback (policy and canary), handoff.

[12:22] Benji Cole: for rollback, do you support automatic fallback to smaller model if large model OOMs?

[12:29] Diego Ramos: yes, you can configure automatic fallback to a quantized or smaller model. also we can set memory thresholds to scale pools.

[12:45] Sarah Kim: audit logging — do you provide immutable logs for compliance?

[12:51] Priya Nair: we can export logs to your S3 with immutability settings, or to your SIEM with retention controls.

[13:05] Tom Alvarez: about cost — what does Dedicated look like cost-wise compared to Hosted?

[13:12] Maya Chen: Dedicated is reserved and typically lower per-token cost but requires a commit; Hosted is pay-as-you-go and easier to start. i'll send a cost estimate as part of the sizing doc; we can also project unit economics with different batch sizes and frequency.

[13:35] Lena Park: can we get a sample estimate for our 50k daily requests pattern?

[13:40] Maya Chen: yes, we'll run the numbers once we have your exact prompt lengths. action: we'll include a cost worksheet.

[14:02] Benji Cole: any constraints on firewall rules or DNS?

[14:08] Diego Ramos: we need outbound TLS to our control plane; for Private you can lock and have local control, but we'll give the precise ports.

[14:25] Maya Chen: okay we're about halfway — want to open for questions from HarborWave?

[14:33] Lena Park: one more — does Redwood support model version pinning and gradual rollouts? we need A/B testing ability.

[14:40] Diego Ramos: yes, rollout policies, canaries, A/B splits, and automatic rollback on quality regressions are built in. we'll show the rollout UI in the demo.

[15:00] Tom Alvarez: do you have a recommended quantization profile for transformer 16B for latency-sensitive inference?

[15:08] Diego Ramos: typically 4-bit quant with block-quantization and KV-cache-friendly layout works well. we recommend benching 4-bit vs 8-bit in your workload; sometimes 4-bit increases CPU decode overhead but reduces GPU memory. we'll include benchmark examples.

[15:32] Sarah Kim: okay last compliance Q — who has access to raw logs on Redwood side? we need role-based access.

[15:40] Priya Nair: access is RBAC-controlled — we can limit to specific Redwood staff and have audit trails. we'll include the access matrix.

[15:58] Maya Chen: great — recap on next steps: i'll send sizing doc + security pack; diego will attach smoke-test harness; lena to share prompt set; tom to confirm network windows and allowlist; sarah to send compliance constraints. schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-07-21.

[16:20] Lena Park: sounds good. a couple of small notes — can you also include a short checklist for our SRE to set up alerts and thresholds?

[16:28] Diego Ramos: yes, i'll include a recommended alerting template (latency thresholds, error rates, queue lengths).

[16:40] Benji Cole: i'll join the smoke-test run and monitor for circuit-breaker behavior.

[16:48] Priya Nair: i'll schedule the recurring syncs and share calendar invites.

[17:05] Maya Chen: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD with the artifacts. last call — any blockers?

[17:12] Sarah Kim: no blockers, just need the security docs.

[17:16] Tom Alvarez: none from networking side aside from timing.

[17:20] Lena Park: no blockers. thanks.

[17:40] Speaker 1: (brief crosstalk) ok bye everyone -- end call.

Notes: occasional stutters and mis-words in transcript (e.g., 'kay em ess' for KMS, 'kv cash' for KV cache). References shared: security pack link (https://redwood.co/security-pack/harborwave-7-14), Dedicated sizing worksheet (link: https://redwood.co/sizing/dedicated-hw-worksheet.xlsx), smoke-test harness (drive link to be attached).

End of transcript.
